title: Copilot Studio: discover and add skills from the skills catalog
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, documented maker flows and package-control requests match the sources checked. It distinguishes the planned catalog from the documented preview and explicitly leaves catalog-specific administration and pricing unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 571880 concerns discovering and adding skills from a catalog in Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: "id": 571880; "title": "Microsoft Copilot Studio: Discover & Add Skills from the skill catalog"

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a catalog in which makers can discover organisational skills.
claims.quote: With the Skills catalog in Copilot Studio, makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills

claims.quote: makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills instead of recreating the same instructions and workflows for every agent.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes selective sharing of approved organisational skills.

claims.quote: The shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store

claims.quote: helping organizations standardize proven ways of working while maintaining centralized governance.

claims.claim: Learn does not identify a Copilot Studio skills catalog by that name or establish that Browse skills is the roadmap catalog.

claims.claim: The available shared skills are those shared by admins or skill owners.
claims.quote: The skills available to you are the ones shared by admins or skill owners.

claims.quote: When you share a skill you created, you and other people in your organization can use it in their Copilot Studio agents.

claims.quote: **Specific users or groups in your organization**: Lets you add people or groups by name or email address. People and groups you add can use the skill.

claims.claim: A skill package can contain supporting scripts, templates and reference documents.
claims.quote: The package can optionally include supporting files, such as scripts, templates, and reference documents.

claims.claim: People and groups receiving a shared skill can add it to their agents.

claims.claim: The cited Learn page does not specify the data-access reach of a catalog skill.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills approval data access harness catalog package management. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-add-existing; these describe instructions and sharing, not data-access boundaries for the roadmap catalog.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-level switch specifically governing the documented maker skill-sharing control was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" admin setting disable sharing tenant. Opened skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule; the latter documents skill-type rules, not a tenant-level maker-sharing switch.

claims.claim: The runtime selects skill activation from the user's message and skill description rather than requiring the user to name it.
claims.quote: The orchestration runtime decides when to activate a skill based on the user's message and the skill's description.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk, impact
claims.claim: An activated skill's instructions guide agent behaviour.
claims.quote: When the runtime activates a skill, the skill's instructions guide your agent's behavior for that specific task.

claims.claim: A skill can instruct an agent to use a specific tool.
claims.quote: For example, a skill might instruct your agent to use a specific tool in a particular way.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an approval step for adding a shared skill beyond the maker's Add action.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "shared skill" "approval". Opened skills-manage; its complete add flow ends with Add and documents no additional approval. Package access-request guidance does not establish a catalog add-approval step.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An edited shared skill must be reshared to make its latest version available to existing recipients.
claims.quote: When you edit and change a skill that you already shared, share the skill again to make the latest version available to those you previously shared it with.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The shared-skill documentation warns that using, building, testing and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness credit charging starts when building starts.
claims.quote: the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence specific to the skills catalog was found in the documentation at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog browsing adding sharing Copilot Credits rate license; "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" admin disable roles licensing. Opened skills-manage, skills-add-existing and billing-credit-overview; no catalog-specific licence is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No catalog-specific credit rate or separate rate for browsing, adding or sharing a skill was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog browsing adding sharing Copilot Credits rate license. Opened skills-manage and billing-credit-overview; reviewed billing-rate search excerpts. They describe harness consumption, not a catalog browse/add/share rate.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Consumption is the documented billing model for the surrounding Microsoft Copilot harness agent experience.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... use a usage-based billing structure.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Variable cost reflects the Copilot Credits meter, which still applies to agents using shared skills.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[0].note; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The skills overview describes Generative and Topic skills for the Customer Conversation harness.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support two types of skills: **Generative** skills ... and **Topic** skills, which are deterministic, authored flows of steps and conditions

claims.claim: The shared-skill page does not explicitly identify which harnesses support Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills approval data access harness catalog package management. Read skills-manage in full and skills-overview: the browse instructions name no supported-harness list; the overview discusses harness-specific creation separately.

claims.claim: Catalog-specific administrator roles are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" "roles". Opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; reviewed authoring-role search results. None assigns roles for the roadmap catalog.

claims.claim: The cited management page names AI Administrator and Global Administrator for MCP request approval, not skill administration.
claims.quote: ## Review and approve MCP requests ... Two roles meet both requirements: ... AI Administrator ... Global Administrator

claims.claim: Package user availability is managed in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools** > **Plugins**. ... Select the plugin that you want to manage. ... Open **Users** ... Managing a skill uses the same actions and steps as managing a plugin

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} with availableTo allowedForSome and allowedUsersAndGroups entries containing resourceType and resourceId sets selected-user availability.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... "resourceType": "user", "resourceId": "5d9fa31e-626e-45fb-b6e7-d8f1f11933a9" ... "resourceType": "group" ... "availableTo": "allowedForSome"

claims.claim: A skill package can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > skill > Block > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools** > **Plugins**. ... From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. ... Select **Block**, and then select **Block** again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a package without a request body.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block ... Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Plugin and separately packaged skill records can be inventoried at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry.
claims.quote: Use **Agents** > **Tools** > **Registry** to review plugin and separately packaged skill records in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: GET /v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages?$filter=elementTypes/any(e:e eq 'AgentSkills') lists packages containing skills.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages ... use the `any` lambda operator on the `elementTypes` collection ... `AgentSkills` | Titles that contain skills.

claims.claim: A maker reaches skill sharing through Build > skill > three dots > Share > Share.
claims.quote: Select the **Build** tab. ... Select the skill you want to share to open the skill configuration panel. ... Select the three dots (**…**) and then select **Share**. ... On the details page, select **Share** in the upper-right corner.

claims.claim: No API for the maker-side skill-sharing operation was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio share skill API PowerShell sharing users groups. Opened skills-manage and the Package Management API overview/update references. The latter govern catalog packages, not the maker-side Share operation.

claims.where: controls[0..2].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that the cited package controls govern the Copilot Studio skills catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills approval data access harness catalog package management; "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog". Opened skills-manage, Package Management API overview and both plugin administration pages; none identifies this catalog's integration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0..1]; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: General package controls allow user scoping and organisation-wide blocking of standalone skill packages.
claims.quote: **Manage user availability** | Selected plugin or standalone skill package. ... **Block** | Selected plugin package and its included agents, or selected standalone skill package. | Prevent users and agents from accessing the package.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A skill bundled inside a package has no individual blocking control; the package's controls apply.
claims.quote: For a bundled skill, apply the plugin's controls. You can't block an individual skill inside a package today.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate component and connection controls.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.

claims.claim: Skills used in Word, Excel and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive rather than the plugin registry.
claims.quote: Don't assume every skill is stored in the plugin registry. Skills used in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive today.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access in Microsoft 365 admin center controls access to plugin publisher categories.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Settings** > **Agent and plugin access**. ... choose which publisher categories users can access: **Microsoft**, **your organization**, or **certified external publishers**.

claims.claim: Package Management API update and block operations are preview.
claims.quote: Update package (preview) | PATCH `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}` ... Block (preview) | POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block`

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters

claims.quote: You can browse and add skills that other people shared with you to your agent. ... On the skill details page, select **Add**. Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" admin setting disable sharing tenant; no catalog-specific enabling switch found.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified catalog arrival behaviour, a required admin action or a catalog-specific admin setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" admin disable roles licensing; "Copilot Studio" "Browse skills" "administrator". Read roadmap, skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule; none specifies the roadmap catalog's rollout default or required admin action.
